With `path`, rows render as buttons with no destination. Used `href` + `@navigate` → `event.preventDefault(); router.push(href)`. 14:52 — **high** (TypeScript): the brief requires a Vite+Vue+**TS** app and the README says "WebKit ships .vue and .ts sources … so vue-tsc --noEmit checks it under strict". In practice `vue-tsc -b` (Vite template's build script) fails with TS2307 "Cannot find module '@aziontech/webkit/app-layout'" for every subpath whose `exports` points at a bare `.vue` file (app-layout, avatar, brand, button, sidebar, tooltip…), while `index.ts/js` ones (menu, command, breadcrumb) resolve. Nothing in README/usage.md tells you what tsconfig makes that work. Workaround: `src/env.d.ts` with `declare module '@aziontech/webkit/*'` (loses all WebKit prop typing) and `noImplicitAny: false` because the blocks are untyped JS `<script setup>` that I converted. 15 min.
14:52 — **low**: the `webkit/authoring-standards` lint demands a *typed* `defineSlots<{…}>()` for any `<slot>`, which forces `lang="ts"` on the shell, while every block ships as plain JS `<script setup>` (so the copied block itself can't hold a slot without a language change).

Also flags the Vite template's own comment in vite.config.ts and the `/// <reference types>` directive in env.d.ts as 'prose comments'. Added `ignores: ['dist/**']` + .stylelintignore. 5 min.

14:54 — **high** (block bug, visible): `first-use` (and `home-dashboard`) draw the mono agent marks (Codex, Cursor) with `:style="{ '--agent-mark': 'url(' + agent.src + ')' }"` + `mask-(--agent-mark)`. Under a default Vite build the small SVGs from `@aziontech/webkit/assets/*.svg` are inlined as `data:image/svg+xml,…` URIs with spaces/quotes, so the unquoted `url(…)` is invalid and the marks render as **solid black squares**. Fixed by quoting: `'url(&quot;' + src + '&quot;)'`. Took 10 min to diagnose.

# DONE — job C1 (console)

Scope (after orchestrator change): 4 pages. App: `app/` (Vite + Vue 3 + TS, Vue Router history mode, `/` lists every page).

## Pages
- `console-overview`: **built**. Remaining differences: the KPI strip is four separate `StatTile`s, where the reference has one card split into 4 cells with the delta right-aligned. Deltas show two decimals ("+12.40%"). Units are uppercased ("/S").
- `console-home-empty`: **built**. Matches the reference at desktop and iPhone: greeting, H1, palette `SearchTrigger`, 3 door cards with `Illustration`, domain check popover, and Copy prompt that toasts "Setup prompt copied.".
- `console-functions-empty`: **built**. Remaining differences: the CLI command field uses the sans face, not mono, and the CLI row uses `pi pi-desktop` because there is no terminal glyph.
- `console-real-time-metrics`: **built**. Remaining differences: the KPI figures use StatTile's mono face where the reference uses a 28 px sans figure, and the chip fill is white instead of grey.

## WebKit pieces used most
`shells/console` block (AppLayout, Sidebar, Menu, GlobalHeader, SearchTrigger, Command, Breadcrumb, ButtonHighlight, Avatar, DropdownMenu, ThemeSwitcher), `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` (default and `empty` variants), `platform/states/first-use`, StatTile, Item / Item.List, Card, EmptyState, LineFigure, Illustration, ChartCard + SparkChart, PageHeader, Chip, Badge, Popover, Button, Input, InputGroupRoot, CopyButton, Link, Tooltip, toast, WebkitProvider, azionicons (`ai ai-*`, `ai-cor ai-*`).

## Top 5 problems with WebKit (by impact)
1. **TypeScript does not work out of the box (high).** With the Vite TS template, `vue-tsc -b` cannot resolve any subpath that is exported as a bare `.vue` file (TS2307). It also fails inside WebKit's own `toast/index.ts` (TS2352 `$toast`). I needed a per-subpath `declare module` shim and a JS re-export for toast, so the app has no WebKit typing at all. A wildcard shim is rejected by `webkit check`.
2. **Block bugs that show on screen (high/medium).**
   - `first-use` and `home-dashboard` build the mono agent marks with an unquoted `url(...)`. Vite inlines the SVGs as `data:` URIs, so the marks render as black squares.
   - `home-dashboard` panel data uses the strings `'false'`, which are truthy, and passes strings to StatTile's number props.
   - Nav nodes use `path`, but Menu only understands `href`.
3. **Blocks vs shell (medium).** The guidelines say to compose the shell once, but every block inlines the whole shell (1,000–2,800 lines) with generic nav. A page can only be built by cutting the body out, which breaks "change only the content" and block-drift tracking. There is also no documented way for a page to open the shell's `Command` palette.
4. **Undocumented sizing and names (medium).**
   - `LineFigure` collapses to 0 px inside `EmptyState #icon` without a sized parent.
   - The figure and illustration names are not listed in the llms docs.
   - `ChartCard` has no llms page or JSON, although it is a public subpath.
   - There is no Router integration guidance for Menu or Breadcrumb.
5. **Missing variants and tooling papercuts (medium/low).**
   - StatTile has no joined/grouped strip, no figure-face option, no delta precision setting, and always uppercases the unit.
   - There is no Button count badge; the Badge has to be hand-positioned as in `split-view`.
   - There is no mono read-only Input.
   - `init` pins devDependencies as "latest" and then warns about it.
   - The init-written ESLint config has no `ignores`, so the pre-commit hook fails on `dist/`.
   - The usage skill shows a `class` override on `Button` that the lint itself forbids.

## Build
`npm run build` (vue-tsc -b && vite build) **passes**. `dist/` works as a static SPA: `vite preview` returned 200 for `/`, every page route and an unknown path. `npx @aziontech/webkit check`: 0 errors, 1 warning (the "latest" pins written by init). ESLint and Stylelint are clean. Every page was shot at the end (desktop + iPhone) with no page errors, and the dev server is stopped.
